_about: Reviewed DATA for aletheia.research: pages that LIST the thing a question asks about, read directly before any search. A web search for events in a city returns encyclopedia pages about the city (2026-10-11, his PC: the city, its hockey team, a TV station), never the listings; these are the listings. An entry applies when one of its `about` phrases is in the question. {city}, {state} and {topic} are filled from the question; an entry whose url needs a place the question does not name uses his own town when `place_default` is "home", and is skipped otherwise. An entry with a `place` applies only to that place. `instead_of` names hosts whose search results are about something else for this kind of question and are dropped. Every page is public and read anonymously; nothing here logs in, signs up, writes or spends. A reviewed edit adds a page; nothing in code names a site or a place. An entry with `places` is not a page: it lists the candidate places for a kind of question that names none, read through the per-place entries; its `ruling` quotes the words that decided what such a place is.
